title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
abstract: arXiv:2611.19822v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Video world models promise to predict the future of a scene from its present. Do current models keep this promise? We probe this question counterfactually. When a small change to the present flips the future, such as a box resting a few millimeters before or past a table edge, a model that tracks the state of the world must flip its prediction too. We build FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks. At the base, visual minimal pairs, two nearly identical frames whose true futures differ, test whether predictions change across the boundary; matched controls go further and test whether they change only where the future does; and dense sweeps, the strictest level, locate exactly where they change. All 11 video world models we evaluate fall short. The best averages 18.3% pair accuracy over real and simulated scenes, below the 25% of random guessing. Mo

translated_title: 翻转测试：视频世界模型未能学习世界状态
translated_abstract: 视频世界模型承诺根据场景的当前状态预测其未来。当前的模型是否兑现了这一承诺？我们通过反事实方法探究这一问题。当对现在的微小改变会翻转未来时——例如一个盒子停在桌沿前几毫米或越过桌沿几毫米的位置——一个真正追踪世界状态的模型也必须相应地翻转其预测。我们构建了FlipTest，这是一个包含三层递进、严格程度逐级提升的测试体系，覆盖来自10个仿真任务和15个真实世界任务的1,680个初始帧。在最基础的层面，视觉最小对（即两帧几乎相同但真实未来不同的画面）用于测试预测是否会跨越边界发生变化；匹配对照进一步测试预测是否仅在真实未来发生变化之处才发生变化；而最严格的密集扫描层则精确定位预测发生变化的位置。我们评估的全部11个视频世界模型均未达标：表现最好的模型在真实与仿真场景上的平均对准确率仅为18.3%，低于随机猜测25%的水平。
tldr: 该论文提出FlipTest反事实测试框架，通过视觉最小对、匹配对照和密集扫描三层递进测试，发现全部11个被评估的视频世界模型都未能真正追踪世界状态——当对当前帧的微小改变会翻转未来时模型预测并未相应翻转，最佳模型的平均对准确率（18.3%）甚至低于随机猜测水平（25%）。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces FlipTest, a three-level counterfactual evaluation framework revealing that all 11 evaluated video world models fail to track the world state—the best model achieves only 18.3% pair accuracy, falling below the 25% of random guessing.
